The wildlife walks team needs helpers on Saturday. Bring gloves and arrive before nine.

Message from a friend
I have booked the woodland trails session for Tuesday, but I may arrive late. Please start without me and save a place.

Information sign
Visitors to the wildlife walks may use the tools, but they must return them before leaving.

Short announcement
The young naturalists meeting has moved from Room 2 to Room 4 because the first room is being painted.

Notice for members
Members can borrow one woodland trails guide for a week. Ask at the desk if you need another copy.

passage.text: When the young naturalists in our town started a wildlife walks project, few residents expected it to grow so quickly. At first, the organisers met in a small room and planned one simple activity involving woodland trails. They soon discovered that people were more willing to join when they could see a clear benefit for the neighbourhood. The organisers therefore published a short timetable and invited local businesses to offer practical help.

The project was not completely easy. Some volunteers were worried that the work would take too much time, while others wanted to change the plan every week. The team solved this by giving each person one small responsibility and reviewing the results together. This made the project feel manageable, and it also meant that new volunteers could contribute without special experience.

Looking back, the organiser says the most important lesson was not the final result but the way people learned to cooperate. The group still has problems, especially when the weather affects outdoor work, yet members now discuss solutions rather than blaming one another. For this reason, the project has become a useful example of how a modest local idea can create lasting connections.

passage.text: The old community centre in our area had been closed for years, and the building was falling apart. (16) ..... A group of residents decided it was time to bring it back to life and create a space where everyone could meet and socialise. The building had been a popular meeting place in the past, but after it closed, people had nowhere to go for social activities, and many residents felt the area had lost its heart.

We formed a committee and applied for a grant from the local council to cover the cost of materials. (17) ..... To our surprise, the application was approved within a month, and we received enough funding to start the renovation work. We organised fundraising events such as cake sales and sponsored walks to raise extra money, and the local community responded generously to our appeals for help.

The renovation work began on a Saturday morning, with volunteers of all ages taking part. (18) ..... Some people painted walls, while others repaired the broken windows and doors, and everyone worked together despite having different skills. The younger volunteers cleaned the garden area at the back, cutting down overgrown bushes and planting new flowers to create a pleasant outdoor space for everyone to enjoy.

The biggest challenge was the old kitchen, which needed new plumbing and electrical wiring throughout. (19) ..... A local plumber offered to do the work at a reduced rate because he believed in the project and wanted to support the community. He spent three weekends installing the new kitchen, working long hours without complaining, and his contribution saved the project thousands of pounds for other improvements.

After six months of hard work by everyone involved, the centre finally reopened. (20) ..... It now hosts art classes, youth clubs and weekly coffee mornings for elderly residents who live alone. The reopening ceremony was attended by over a hundred people, including the mayor, and the event was covered by the local television news channel that evening.

passage.text: Our environmental club organised a beach clean-up last Sunday morning. More (21) ..... fifty volunteers showed up, including families with young children who wanted to help. Everyone was given gloves and a bag, and (22) ..... asked to separate plastic from other rubbish to make recycling easier. Within two hours, we had collected over a hundred kilograms of waste from the sand. It was shocking (23) ..... see how much rubbish had accumulated on such a beautiful and popular beach. A local café provided free drinks for (24) ..... the volunteers as a thank-you gesture for their hard work. The event was (25) ..... successful that we have decided to make it a monthly activity for the club. If we want to protect our coastline, we need to take action (26) ..... than wait for others to do it for us. Several local businesses have offered to sponsor future clean-up events, and the council has promised to install more rubbish bins along the beach to make it easier for visitors to dispose of their waste properly. We recorded the results after each clean-up and sent them to the council. The figures helped officials identify the areas where litter returned fastest and place bins in better positions.

We ate our sandwiches while sitting on a large rock, watching birds fly (30) ........ the valley below us in the sunshine. On the way down, my friend twisted (31) ........ ankle on a loose stone, so we had to walk slowly and carefully. Despite the pain, she kept making jokes, which made (32) ........ all laugh and forget about the difficulty of the walk. The hiking trip brought my friends and me closer together, and we have already started planning our next adventure, which will be a longer three-day hike in a more remote mountainous area.
